prompt: Could you review PR #142 before it merges? It adds our reporting feature to the Terraform repo: a reporting database, an export bucket, a static website bucket and a role for the reporting tasks. The PR description is review/PR-142.md, and the PR is already applied in this tree, so the files it lists are the changed ones. I want to know what in it is risky and what to change before it goes to production. Write the review in REVIEW.md and end it with one fenced json block: a list of findings, each with file, line (a number, approximate is fine), severity (critical, high, medium or low), issue and fix. Do not change any other file.
twinIdea: Add a new reporting module to the Terraform codebase with a database, S3 bucket, and IAM role, writing the infrastructure code from scratch.

verdicts.note: The prompt asks for a security review and specifies the review format, but it names no particular threat method, framework, or work process.
The REVIEW.md location, fenced JSON fields, approximate line numbers, severity vocabulary, and intended public decoys are clear from the prompt and fixture.

Fix round (author) removed the answer comments and made decoy and padding tests fail on an empty answer (0 of 14 pass on the fixture). The lead removed the security notes that listed two of the defects.

No hidden test requires information unavailable to a careful engineer: the relevant values, paths, intended exceptions, and requested output fields are present in the fixture and PR diff. The severity thresholds are defensible for the exposed database, credentials, IAM, KMS, storage, and audit issues.

Comments such as Should be true, seeded issue and Overly permissive were removed in the fix round; the lead removed the defect list from docs/reporting.md and the hand-written diff, which did not apply to the tree.

items.text: Explains that a password given as a variable default also lands in plan output and state, and recommends a secret store reference plus sensitive variables, not only removing the default.
Notes that CI runs only fmt and validate and suggests an IaC security scan in the pipeline so these issues are caught before review.
Rejects the PR note that broad access will be tightened before production as a reason to merge, since the same modules feed both environments.
Recommends account-level blocking of public bucket access as a guardrail, with the intended public website as an explicit exception.
Flags the reporting database settings that risk data loss (deletion protection off, final snapshot skipped) as a lower-severity item separate from exposure.
Says which findings block the merge and which can follow, so the author knows what to fix first.

rubric.criterion: Findings are clearly explained with specific file references and actionable fixes (code cannot check this because it requires judgment of explanation quality)

Critical and high severity issues are correctly identified and prioritized. Fail: critical issues missing from the top of the list, or decoys ranked high. Partial: critical issues found, but ordered below lower-severity ones or with severities off by more than one level. Pass: the critical and high issues come first with defensible severities, and decoys are absent or marked low with a reason. (code cannot check this because severity assessment requires security expertise)
